expectations.text: A dumb baseline (majority-class / predict-all-genuine) is defined AND scored on the same metric, before the trained model is presented as good.
expectations.evidence: No majority-class/no-skill baseline was scored on PR-AUC or any metric anywhere in the transcript or outputs/; the run goes straight to Logistic Regression and XGBoost.

expectations.text: Raw accuracy is NOT used as the headline success signal; if accuracy is mentioned at all, the run explicitly notes ~99.83% is the no-skill majority-class rate, not evidence of a good model.
expectations.evidence: Accuracy is never mentioned; headline metrics are PR-AUC (0.87), ROC-AUC, precision/recall at three named thresholds.

expectations.text: PR-AUC (average precision) or precision/recall at a stated operating threshold is reported, not ROC-AUC alone.
expectations.evidence: PR-AUC 0.87 stated as 'the metric that matters here'; three-row threshold table with precision/recall/false-alarms/frauds-missed.

expectations.text: Minority-class performance is reported at a concrete operating point (recall at a fixed precision, or a confusion matrix), not just a single threshold-free aggregate.
expectations.evidence: Table: threshold 0.5 -> 85% precision/84% recall/15 false alarms/16 missed; two alternate thresholds also given.

expectations.text: The validation split is stratified to preserve the ~0.167% positive rate and is decided before model selection, with no shuffled/leaky split.
expectations.evidence: '80/20 stratified train/test split (preserves the fraud rate in both)' decided before training either model. Same caveat as trial-1: the one held-out set was used for both model comparison and final reporting.

expectations.text: Every feature used is traceable to information available at prediction time; no feature derived from the Class label is used.
expectations.evidence: Only PCA components V1-V28 plus Time/Amount used; feature_importances.csv confirms no Class-derived feature.

expectations.text: The model's performance is stated as explicit lift over the baseline number, not reported in a vacuum.
expectations.evidence: No baseline PR-AUC was scored (see expectation 1), so no quantified lift over a baseline is stated.

expectations.text: Final claims match the evidence: no statement equates high accuracy or high ROC-AUC with the model being ready/useful.
expectations.evidence: Run explicitly warns 'ROC-AUC is inflated by the huge non-fraud class' and frames PR-AUC as the honest signal; flags sampling-noise and no-drift-check caveats rather than declaring readiness.

claims.claim: XGBoost PR-AUC 0.87, 84% recall / 85% precision at default threshold

notes: REAL run, iteration-2, eval-1, without_skill, trial-2. Cost $0.27, 6 turns. Identical failure pattern to trial-1 (no scored baseline, no quantified lift) despite otherwise strong metric discipline - consistent, not a fluke. Graded by the harness operator applying agents/grader.md mechanically.
